answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring a refundable stake before an agent can trade: each identity locks funds that are slashed if peers detect duplicate or dishonest behavior. Like basalt, the stake is hard to forge cheaply, so creating thousands of fake accounts costs real capital, while honest agents keep their deposit and build reputation over a long horizon. The stake turns every voyage into a trade into an audited commitment, so a sybil attack must pay for every identity it creates.
